zip_caveats: A ZIP doesn't tell us your districts here. Davidson County is split among three U.S. House districts (4, 6 and 7, redrawn in May 2026), and only state Senate Districts 17, 19 and 21 have races this year, so some Nashville voters have no state Senate race. Your districts are on the yellow voter card the Election Commission mailed this summer, after the May 2026 redraw, on your sample ballot, or in the state's district lookup. Belle Meade, Forest Hills and Goodlettsville voters also vote for city commissioners, and Goodlettsville votes on a sales tax question; those are only on those cities' ballots. Some ZIPs cross the county line, and the other county's ballot has different races: 37072 (Goodlettsville) reaches into Sumner and Robertson counties; 37076 (Hermitage) and 37138 (Old Hickory) reach into Wilson County; 37080 (Joelton) reaches into Cheatham County; 37215 and 37221 (Bellevue) reach into Williamson County; 37209 touches Cheatham County. If your voter card names another county, this is not your ballot. Small parts of 37015, 37027 (mostly Brentwood), 37064, 37086, 37122, 37135 and 37143 are in Davidson County too but open their own county's ballot; if you vote in Davidson with one of those ZIPs, choose Nashville from the list of places.

early_in_person.hours_note: Davidson County: Wednesday, October 14 through Thursday, October 29, at any of 15 early voting sites. situations.answer: The deadline to ask for an absentee ballot was Saturday, October 24. If yours hasn't come, call the Davidson absentee office at 615-862-8815. Today, Thursday, October 29, is the last day of early voting: any of 15 sites, 8 AM to 7 PM. On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, vote at your own polling place, 7 AM to 7 PM.
steps: Call the absentee office, 615-862-8815 (Monday to Friday, 8 AM to 4:30 PM), and ask how to vote in person instead.
See whether your ballot was sent or received: the state's Voter Registration Lookup at tnmap.tn.gov/voterlookup.
Already filled it in? Mail it so it arrives by 7 PM on November 3. Tennessee doesn't let you hand it in at a polling place or the office.

situations.short: On Nov 3 you must vote at your assigned polling place; the county's Polling Place Finder shows it.
situations.answer: On Election Day, Davidson County voters must vote at their assigned polling place. Find yours with the Polling Place Finder (maps.nashville.gov/PollingPlaceFinder) or call 615-862-8800. One place changed this year: voters assigned to the Downtown Library (District 19, Precinct 5) vote at the Howard Office Building, 700 President Ronald Reagan Way.
steps: Moved within Davidson County and didn't update your address? Go to the polling place for your new address on Election Day; you can change your address there and vote.
At the wrong place? Ask the poll workers for your right one, and go there before 7 PM.

notes: Today, Thursday, October 29, is the last day of early voting: any of 15 sites, 8 AM to 7 PM. On Election Day, Tuesday, November 3, polls are open 7 AM to 7 PM, and you must vote at your assigned polling place. One change this year: voters assigned to the Downtown Library (District 19, Precinct 5) vote at the Howard Office Building, 700 President Ronald Reagan Way. Bring a Tennessee or federal photo ID; it can be expired, but college IDs and out-of-state licenses don't count. Absentee ballots go back by mail only and must arrive by 7 PM on November 3. Your U.S. House district may be new this year: the state redrew the lines in May 2026, and the yellow voter card mailed this summer shows the new one.
